Implementer's four self-doubts all checked out: (1) DSN skip is real and I supplied a DB; (3) 'null' staying a 200 no-op is genuinely indistinguishable from '{}' after a successful decode, so leaving it is correct for this scope; (4) both webapp callers (compat.ts:336 patchMyValues, :348 patchUserValues) always JSON-serialize a small well-formed map, so no in-tree client breaks and webapp needed no gate (0 web changes).

Doubt (2) is the one real soft spot, non-blocking: 'a refused patch leaves no audit row' proves a negative inside a 3.2s poll window. It cannot produce a false FAIL (it only fails if a row appears), but it can produce a false PASS if a row ever arrived later, and it adds ~3.2s fixed to the package. The positive control (waitForAuditRow on target 'user-audit-ok', count==1, no target collision with the earlier '' / 'user-a' rows) is correctly built and does make the zero-count meaningful.

Compat/release-note item: a malformed or over-cap body on these two routes now answers 400/413 where it answered 200 before, under a NEW error id api.custom_profile.values.patch.invalid_body that is not an upstream Mattermost id. Existing ids and the 200 response shape are untouched, and each handler has exactly one route (router.go:1014/1016), so blast radius is those two routes only — but a third-party client that relied on the tolerated 200 would now see a failure. Worth one release-note line.

Security review (no block, no attack path): auth and authz are untouched and both still run BEFORE the new decode — requireUserParamAccess on the per-user route, the uid=="" 401 on the global one. No new identifier, route, role, secret, crypto comparison, or dependency; the change only narrows accepted input. The 400 detail is a json decoder message (one offending character or a Go type name), not request content, and matches the decodeCollectionBody pattern already used across the package. Net positive for access review: the admin-backfills-another-user path no longer writes a count:0 audit row for a write that never happened.

Legal/privacy review (no block): no new personal data collected, stored, or transmitted; no change to retention, purpose, access control, or cross-border transfer for custom profile values. Test fixtures are synthetic (audit-ok@example.test) with no production data in the test schema, and the new error id makes no external promise.
